Share of the evidence each study and design contributes

Source: R/diagnostics.R
information_share.Rd

Inverse-variance weights on the random-effects scale, \(w_i \propto 1/(s_i^2 + \tau_\theta^2)\), normalised to sum to one. The answer to "which studies is this result actually resting on?", which a table of estimates never shows.

Usage

information_share(fit)

Arguments

fit

A meta_did() fit with summary-level studies.

Value

A data frame with one row per study: study_id, design, se, weight (summing to one), ordered by decreasing weight.

Details

\(s_i\) is the design-appropriate sampling SD of that study's effect estimate: the double-difference SE for DiD, the change-score SE for pre-post, the arm-contrast SE for post-only. \(\tau_\theta\) is taken at its posterior median.

This is an approximation in one respect worth knowing: it ignores the coupling through the nuisance parameters, so a post-only study's weight is slightly overstated relative to a DiD study's, since part of its information is spent on \(\gamma\). omega_pp() computes the exact two-design version. Summary-level data only.

See also

plot_information_share(), omega_pp()
